name: Barabbas
title: The Freed Prisoner
summary: Barabbas was a Jewish prisoner who was imprisoned for rebellion and murder when Jesus was brought to trial. He was released by Pontius Pilate instead of Jesus, as the crowd chose to spare him during the Passover festival. His release has become a powerful symbol of substitutionary salvation.

keyEvents.title: Imprisoned for Rebellion and Murder
keyEvents.description: Barabbas was in prison for participating in an uprising in Jerusalem and for committing murder during the unrest.

keyEvents.title: The Crowd Chooses Barabbas
keyEvents.description: When Pilate gave the people the choice to release Jesus or Barabbas, they shouted that Barabbas should be freed and Jesus crucified.

keyEvents.title: Barabbas Released Instead of Jesus
keyEvents.description: Pilate granted the crowd's request and released Barabbas, while handing Jesus over to be crucified. Barabbas went free while the innocent one took his place.

keyEvents.title: The Passover Amnesty Tradition
keyEvents.description: It was customary for the Roman governor to release a prisoner at the people's request during the Passover festival, which made Barabbas' release possible.
